# Bitlync

One API for ISVs. Write once. Connect to many MSPs.

Site: https://www.bitlync.com/
Human docs: https://www.bitlync.com/docs
Security: https://www.bitlync.com/security
Legal: https://www.bitlync.com/legal/terms
Privacy: https://www.bitlync.com/legal/privacy
MSP connect terms: https://www.bitlync.com/legal/connect-terms

## Sandbox

- Public sandbox host: https://bitlync-sandbox-demo.onrender.com
- Demo key is on https://www.bitlync.com/docs#docs-quickstart
- Fixture data only. Not a customer tenant. Not production AWS.
- GET /tenants/sandbox-mainstreet/tickets returns 200 and sandbox: true.
- There is no public live-read URL for a real MSP.
- No production host printed here besides the sandbox.
- This page does not document a vendor daily cap.
- No public ops host on this page.
- There is no public MCP host.
- The ISV does not paste MSP creds. There is no shared-secret path that puts PSA keys in your app.

## Writes and refusals

- dry_run defaults true. A dry run does not create a ticket.
- We do not mint an agreement header. We do not mint a project header.
- Company create is off unless the MSP turns it on for your grant. We always match first. If two records match, we refuse.
- Device write is off unless the MSP turns it on for your grant. We never auto-create an unmatched company.
- Tickets are two-way when the MSP grants it. You can create, update, and close. You can subscribe to events when the MSP changes the ticket in their PSA.
- When a device or company is created or updated, you can list those events or get a signed webhook.
- Close defaults off unless the MSP turns it on.
- A parked write is 501, not a generic 500.

## MCP

MCP exposes the same read model. Writes stay on REST until the grant and dry-run path is identical.
